title: A cloud epic run writes no run events and never leaves 'starting'
description:
An epic run on the deployed factory is invisible to every surface built to watch it. Observed on run_ba1cc951cd184126b7c9e3c54fecc5c2 (epic uzc) while it was demonstrably working:

    ticfac cloud status   state: starting
    ticfac events         "the run has not written an event - which is what a run that has not started looks like"
    wrangler tail         POST /api/branches; 6 x chat/completions; 8 x RepoRoom.publish; renewSlot; renewDispatchLease

The run was cutting its integration branch, calling GLM, publishing commits through the room and renewing its leases. Both supported surfaces said it had not started.

Mechanism: src/run-events.ts is imported by src/run-workflow.ts and src/run-room.ts, and NOT by src/epic-reconciler.ts. run-events even exports an epicStarted() helper that nothing on the epic path calls. So k7p built the feed, wired it to the OLD driver, and the driver Phase 5 ships emits nothing into it. The run row likewise never leaves `starting`.

This is the exact question the operator asked when k7p was filed - "as an epic runs in the cloud exclusively after phase 5, how do i track status while it runs?" - and on the cloud path the answer today is: you cannot, unless you have wrangler and the account.

Note k7p is not wrong about the LOCAL host: `ticfac events epic-dha --follow` works and is how the local Phase 5 run was watched all day. It is the cloud half that is missing.

Do:
- emit the same event vocabulary from the epic reconciler: run started, tick dispatched, gate started/failed, tick closed, run finished, and the interventions supervision records.
- move the run row out of `starting` when the first pass dispatches.
- b8p is the sibling for `ticfac cloud supervisor`, which is blind to the same driver. Fixing the feed does not fix that; fix both.

Found by performing u9h.
acceptance_criteria: ticfac events --follow on a cloud epic run shows dispatches, gates, closes and interventions as they happen, and cloud status leaves 'starting' once the first pass dispatches
